# The Silence Between the Stars

## Scripture
*"Be still, and know that I am God."* — Psalm 46:10 (NIV)

## Reflection
On a clear November night, when you look up between the bright constellations, you'll notice something: the darkness itself. The gaps. The vast, quiet spaces where no star shines. We tend to focus on the points of light—Polaris, Orion's belt, the dazzling planets—but most of the sky is empty stillness.

That emptiness isn't nothing. It's the canvas that makes the light visible. Without the dark spaces, the stars would blur into one indistinguishable glow. The silence between the stars is what lets each one speak.

Our lives are like that sky. We fixate on the bright moments—the answered prayers, the joyful seasons, the times when God's presence feels obvious. But the quiet stretches between? The waiting, the ordinary days, the unanswered questions? Those aren't failures of faith. They're the space that lets us see God's lights more clearly.

Psalm 46 was written in chaos—nations raging, kingdoms falling. And right in the middle of the noise, God speaks: *Be still.* Not because nothing is happening, but because He is happening, even in the silence.

This fall, when the night sky stretches wide and dark, don't rush past the stillness. Let it do its work. The God who set each star in place also set you here—and He is not absent in the quiet.

## Prayer
Lord, teach me to treasure the stillness as much as the light. When the sky feels empty and Your voice seems distant, help me trust that You are still here, still working, still God. Thank You for the holy quiet that makes Your glory visible. Amen.
